chapters.title: The Expensive Claim
chapters.blurb: Here are two sentences about the same checkout page: it is broken, and it works. They look symmetrical. They are not.

chapters.title: Every Run Is a Recording
chapters.blurb: A test run starts with a journey — a scripted intention. This one belongs to the Acme store: add an item to the cart, check out, and pay.

chapters.title: The Agent Reads the Tape
chapters.blurb: The run is over. The browser is gone. What remains is the tape — and one question: what actually happened in there?

chapters.title: A Finding Carries Its Proof
chapters.blurb: Believing an app is broken costs almost nothing — the worst case of checking a bug report is a few wasted minutes. So a finding has exactly one job: survive the checking.

chapters.title: Green Must Be Proven
chapters.blurb: A webhook arrives: someone says the checkout bug is fixed. Notice what kind of claim that is. Fixed is the expensive kind — it gets recorded, but it does not get believed yet.
